questions.learningObjective: evaluate weight and color hierarchy in a design critique
questions.stem: On Weight and color hierarchy: a designer reviewing a school district's newsletter notices that a designer must emphasize a label without changing its size. Which alternative cue would work effectively?

options.text: Reduce the leading around only that particular label
options.misconception: mistakes a local line spacing change for emphasis

options.text: Increase the gutter immediately beside the label
options.misconception: confuses a layout gap with typographic emphasis

options.text: Increase the weight or apply a contrasting color to the label

questions.learningObjective: evaluate signs and symbols in a design critique
questions.stem: On Signs and symbols: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that an icon relies on a literal picture to communicate an action. Which distinction describes a more abstract mark?

options.text: A sign and a symbol are identical in every single respect
options.misconception: denies a distinction that semioticians actually make

options.text: A symbol works by convention or analogy rather than literal resemblance
A symbol must always take the form of a photograph
options.misconception: misstates what a symbol can be in visual communication

options.text: A sign never needs to be learned by its audience at all
options.misconception: overstates the difference between signs and symbols

questions.explanation: A sign often resembles or directly indicates what it means, while a symbol communicates through convention or analogy and may need to be learned. Choosing between them affects how quickly an audience understands an interface icon.
questions.hint: Does the mark look like the thing, or stand for it by convention?
